Kowalski goes to the ocean to investigate coral reef ecosystems. For this project, she starts with the First Step, a condition for corals to flourish. Here, she assesses the state of the reef with scuba-rogue planes and submersible analyses, enabling her to dredge up reefs in depth. Dr. Kowski reviews what she sees there, from the bottom to the base of the reef. Using underwater microscopes and acoustic imaging, she proceeds to analyze the depth and breadth on a deep seafloor a.k.a. the new reef at Trinidad and Tobago National Park through the eyes of a user-friendly diver. She predicts that within five years, 50 percent of the reef will be unexplored and nearly 25 percent will develop dead reef edges. Over 1.2 million tourists visit the region each year. Dr. Kowski believes that a similar rate of destruction to the Great Barrier Reef restoration system not only will occur, it will also lead to a corresponding threat to the reef.
